name: Hydrogen
notes: Recognised as a distinct 'inflammable air'; named by Lavoisier 1783

name: Helium
notes: Solar spectral line 1868; terrestrial isolation by Ramsay 1895

name: Beryllium
notes: Oxide identified 1798; metal by Wohler and Bussy 1828

name: Carbon
notes: Known as charcoal and diamond since antiquity

name: Nitrogen
notes: Noxious air; also Scheele and Cavendish independently

name: Oxygen
notes: Scheele prepared 1771 but published 1777; Priestley published 1774

name: Fluorine
notes: Recognised as an element in hydrofluoric acid 1810; isolated by Moissan 1886

name: Magnesium
notes: Magnesia recognised as distinct 1755; metal by Davy 1808

name: Aluminium
notes: Impure metal 1825; Wohler produced purer metal 1827

name: Silicon
notes: Gay-Lussac and Thenard made impure silicon 1811

name: Phosphorus
notes: First element with a documented individual discoverer

name: Chlorine
notes: Scheele isolated the gas but thought it a compound; Davy showed it elemental 1810

name: Argon
notes: First noble gas found on Earth

name: Vanadium
notes: Del Rio withdrew his claim; rediscovered by Sefstrom 1830

name: Manganese
discoverer: Johan Gottlieb Gahn / C. W. Scheele

name: Zinc
notes: Smelted in India by c.1300; isolated in Europe by Marggraf 1746

name: Arsenic
notes: Compounds used in antiquity; elemental form described c.1250

name: Niobium
notes: Called columbium; confirmed distinct from tantalum by Rose 1844

name: Technetium
notes: Confirmed Mendeleev's eka-manganese; first synthetic element

name: Lutetium
discoverer: Georges Urbain / Carl Auer von Welsbach
notes: Priority contested between Urbain and Welsbach

name: Hafnium
discoverer: Dirk Coster and George de Hevesy

name: Tungsten
notes: Acid identified 1781; metal by the Elhuyar brothers 1783

name: Platinum
notes: Pre-Columbian use in South America; described in Europe 1735-1748

name: Bismuth
notes: Known as a metal by c.1400; shown distinct from lead by Geoffroy 1753

name: Radon
notes: Thorium emanation 1899; radium emanation by Dorn 1900

name: Einsteinium
discoverer: Ghiorso et al (Argonne Los Alamos Berkeley)
notes: Found in H-bomb debris; publication delayed by secrecy

name: Fermium
discoverer: Ghiorso et al (Argonne Los Alamos Berkeley)
notes: Found in H-bomb debris; publication delayed by secrecy

name: Mendelevium
discoverer: Ghiorso Harvey Choppin Thompson and Seaborg

name: Nobelium
notes: Contested between Stockholm Berkeley and Dubna; IUPAC credits Dubna

name: Lawrencium
notes: Credit shared between Berkeley and Dubna

name: Nihonium
notes: IUPAC awarded priority to RIKEN in 2015
